note: Investor-friendly title companies and closing attorneys (public business contacts). B-22 / D-037 Title Companies tab. status: not_called = nobody has confirmed by phone yet. Ask each: (1) Do you close assignments? (2) Same-day double closes, incl. transactional funding? (3) Fees and clear-to-close speed?
lessons: Big national underwriters (Chicago Title, First American) often avoid simultaneous double closings; small independent or attorney-owned agencies with investor teams are the reliable partners.
North Carolina closes through attorneys, not title companies; since 2021 every party must sign off on an assignment.
Before using one: ask for a sample settlement statement (to see fees) and how many double closes they did last month.

Remote signing: Florida treats remote online notarization as normal; in Texas RON generally works for cash deals (lenders often refuse it). Mail-away signing abroad may need a US consulate notary or apostille: ask the title company.

FIRPTA: if the seller is a foreign person (not a US citizen or green-card holder), the buyer/title company may have to withhold 15% of the sale price. Ask a lawyer/CPA how this affects double closes and assignment fees before the first deal.
